terms.comment: Post-Augustan prose (Curtius, Pliny), and the Vulgate’s Poenitentiam agite, in the Clementine’s spelling. Repentance is paenitentia (Liv., Tac.).
Impersonal: mē peccātī paenitet, I repent of my sin, with the accusative of the person and the genitive of the thing (see I’m sorry).

phrases.latin: Poenitentiam agite: appropinquāvit enim rēgnum caelōrum.
phrases.english: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

phrases.latin: Imprūdēns peccat, quem post factī paenitet.
phrases.english: He who is sorry afterwards did wrong without thinking.
we are vexed, ashamed and sorry (the morning’s regret)

sources: Lewis & Short: paenitentia · Lewis & Short: paeniteo
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-publilius, loci-prudentius), checked against the editions named there.
Vulgate verses checked against the Clementine Vulgate (CrossWire VulgClementine, via the scrollmapper bible_databases repository) and Hetzenauer’s edition, in Clementine spelling.
